summary: A 1866 North Channel light at Red Rock Point, Killarney: keepers from 1867, a 1909 square wooden tower still standing, and a 1956 capsizing rescue.

light.fog_signal: horn, 3 s blast with 27 s silence (Coast Guard list)

structures.type: square-tapered wooden tower with octagonal iron lantern
structures.note: Coast Guard list gives 9.1 m. The Department's 1910 works list gives a 29-foot tower, and the Register gives 1909.

First tower at Red Rock: about 20 ft (6.1 m) to the top of the birdcage lantern (Lighthouse Friends). Darius Smith's 1876 description, as printed by Lighthouse Friends, gives 14 ft (4.3 m) for the building.

staffing.note: The Lighthouse Friends head keeper list runs to Alfred de Lamorandiere from 1982, with no end date. Whether resident keeping ended is not stated in these sources.

access.note: Canadian Coast Guard property. Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends). Reached by a one-lane gravel road off Ontario Street; parking limited, motor homes not advised.

events.note: Five nearly identical North Channel lights built in 1866, two of them at Killarney (Red Rock and Partridge Island).
Station first lit 1867 (Lighthouse Friends). The station record gives 1866, from a directory's station-established date.
Inspection by Darius Smith, Superintendent of Lights above Montreal; as Lighthouse Friends prints his report, the lower light's keeper had been away over two years and his sons kept the lights.
Pierre Regis de Lamorandiere appointed after Proulx was superannuated in September 1880.
Frank Roque appointed at Killarney on 28 February 1905 (Department list). Lighthouse Friends gives 1904.

Present square-tapered wooden tower built, 1909 (Register; Lighthouse Friends gives cost $782.29). The Department's report for the year ended 30 June 1910 lists the 29-foot tower at Killarney east, and another at Killarney west.
Keeper Ferdinand Solomon's boat capsized in breakers in November 1956; he reached Jackman Shoal and was brought in by a local game warden (Lighthouse Friends).
Fog whistle installed at the tower; a hand foghorn had served the east light until then (Lighthouse Friends).
Highway 637 completed; access to Killarney had been limited to boats (Lighthouse Friends).
Recognized Federal Heritage Building; date recognized 5 September 1991 (Register no. 9685).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends says the five North Channel lights were built in 1866 and that the station was first lit in 1867. The station record's 1866 comes from a directory's station-established date. This story uses 1867 for first light and 1866 for the building of the first towers.

The present tower is dated 1909 by the Register and by Lighthouse Friends. The Department's works list for the year ended 30 June 1910 records the erection of the 29-foot towers at Killarney east and west. The work probably ran across 1909 and 1910.

notes_for_editor: Read: Lighthouse Friends (copyrighted; paraphrased, short quotations only), the Heritage Guide copy of Register entry 9685, the Canadian Coast Guard list (entry 974), and Department of Marine reports in the corpus (fiscal 1906, 1909, 1910, 1911). No newspaper search was usable: 'Killarney' is a common name and the Chronicling America hits did not concern the lights. Darius Smith's 1876 report and the 1866 contract are not in the corpus (which starts in fiscal 1900) and are cited through Lighthouse Friends. Disagreements left open: first lit 1867 (Lighthouse Friends) vs 1866 (record); Frank Roque's start 1904 (Lighthouse Friends) vs appointment 28 February 1905 (Department list, matched by position in an OCR table); the tower's date 1909 (Register and Lighthouse Friends) vs the Department's year-ended-1910 works list; tower height 9.1 m (Coast Guard list) vs 14 ft (Smith, via Lighthouse Friends, for the 1876 building) vs about 20 ft to the lantern top (Lighthouse Friends). Named keeper 'Killarney West' (Department 1910) is 'Killarney Northwest' on the Coast Guard list and Partridge Island in Lighthouse Friends. Omitted on purpose: the 1880s dispute over Lamorandiere's ancestry and annuity (Lighthouse Friends prints it at length; not needed for the station's history and contested), and the family circumstances of the 1950 station swap and the 1956 rescue (private family matters). The 1950s-1980s keepers (Solomon, Roque, Burke, Sinclair, Skipen, Alfred de Lamorandiere) are post-1960 or late in the period; only their public roles and years appear. Henry Solomon (1880s acting keeper, Lighthouse Friends) shares a surname with Ferdinand Solomon; no source links them, so none is assumed. Staffing end date and any automation date are not in these sources. Dept 1909 table: Frank Roque's appointment read by position (station, name, date, salary columns). Cost $782.29 is cited to Lighthouse Friends only; not found in the OCR table. Fact-check 2026-10-27: 'Sudbury District' was removed (no cited source gives it); the story now uses Lighthouse Friends' 'roughly seventy-five kilometres southwest of Sudbury'. Frank Roque's 28 February 1905 appointment was confirmed on the page images for the 1906 list (scan 174), the 1909 list (scan 177) and the 1911 list (scan 254). The 1910 entry for the 29-foot tower at Killarney east is verbatim (scan 86). Pilot and Solomon's role changed from acting keeper to other, since Lighthouse Friends says only that they looked after the light. The isophase description was removed (not in the Coast Guard entry).
